name: render-path-budget
description: Limits per landing surface for a first-time mobile visitor who doesn't scroll, checked by ./bench.sh budget (Lighthouse on the generator, median of the runs). A limit is a measured value plus a margin, so the budget passes today and fails on a regression. Byte limits are in bytes. targets holds what counts as good and never fails a run. cpu_slowdown is Lighthouse's CPU slowdown that the LCP, TBT, and score limits are calibrated for: a run with another one fails those lines. See docs/benchmarks/viral-spike-render-path-budget.md.

home.note: The start page (docs/implementation/start-page-redesign.md): a search over the painted room, Where to start below. Recalibrated 2026-10-29 from a local production build behind TLS and HTTP/2 with 103 hints (CPU-capped mobile Lighthouse, 9 runs each, the old TV page measured the same way): images 17 -> 59 and image bytes 94 KB -> 853 KB (the shelf covers, the card's fan and the browse rails' posters, all after the room), total bytes 688 KB -> 1.24 MB, render-blocking 5 -> 6 (five page sheets), while scripts went 42 -> 34 and script bytes 534 -> 341 KB and HTML stays 29 KB; those caps are unchanged. LCP and score caps are unchanged until a generator run calibrates them. Selected composer and history-return state (2026-11-02): unchanged main measured 329.7 KiB of first-view script locally versus 325.2 KiB with the selected design, above the old 295 KiB cap. Reserve 344 KiB for the needed first-view composer/history code and existing baseline. Start-page styles now share one bundle; the decorative fan reuses w185 shelf posters on phones. Timing and layout limits remain unchanged.

movie.note: Opened-demand first-view transport reserves 1 KiB of script and total bytes; matched browser measurement adds 859 script bytes. Other caps retain their existing calibration. Title page redesign (2026-11-04): the new sections' first-view code (the rail's way-in tabs, Feels the same's print and stepper, the shelves, find across the sub-pages, the sub-page way in) adds 21.7 KiB of brotli script and one script file over origin/main in a local build (every static chunk of the route; the rows' content, the expanded shelves and the quick view load on first use); the HTML shrinks by about 9 KiB compressed. Script and total bytes +22 KiB, script count +1. At a glance rows in the first HTML (2026-11-04): the rows' content is in the server HTML, closed rows hidden, so its code joins the route's static chunks instead of loading on the first open: +4.7 KiB brotli script, no new file, in a local build over origin/main; the HTML grows by about 4-5 KiB brotli (The Matrix 35.3 -> 40.2 KiB, Breaking Bad 35.5 -> 39.1 KiB on the dev server) and stays under its cap. Script bytes +5 KiB, total bytes +10 KiB. Character portraits (2026-11-06): local production builds of the branch and origin/main 5660d441c measured with ./bench.sh budget --where local, 3 runs each (both builds fail the same lines locally: no static host, local data). The feature adds two small first-view chunks (portraits 1.3 KiB and parts 0.6 KiB brotli: the cast faces, the person page's Characters shelf and Discover's roles strip render in the first HTML, so they can't wait for an interaction; the character quick view itself loads on first use) and the quick view's provider in the shell (+0.9 KiB). Measured over origin/main: +5.8 KiB script, +2 scripts, +4 requests (the two chunks and the portraits read). Script bytes +6 KiB, total bytes +8 KiB, script count +2, host requests +4.
